mechanism_narrative: Sustained decline in WORKPLACES mobility over four consecutive weeks signals persistent remote work adoption or economic contraction. This reduces commuter-adjacent retail visits, driving RETAIL_REC further negative over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES declined from -12.3% to -15.1% over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days exceeds RETAIL_REC mean over last 28 days despite WORKPLACES remaining below -12%.

mechanism_narrative: Accelerating RESIDENTIAL mobility increase (6.4% to 8.0% over four weeks) indicates households spending more time at home. This substitutes away from retail-and-recreation visits, suppressing RETAIL_REC growth or deepening decline over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 percentage points over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL remains above 7.5%.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility decline exceeds -20% in the most recent week, signaling reduced public transport use. When transit falls below -20%, outdoor and retail mobility typically contract further within one week as accessibility constraints bind.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -20% in current week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases week-on-week in the first week after TRANSIT crosses below -20%.

mechanism_narrative: Joint decline in PARKS and TRANSIT mobility signals reduced outdoor activity and transport access. When both fall simultaneously, retail-and-recreation visits decline because consumers lack both motivation and means to visit retail venues, suppressing RETAIL_REC over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS and TRANSIT both decline week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at -38.9% and TRANSIT at -20.3% in t-0w, both declining from prior weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days when PARKS and TRANSIT are both below -20%.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility decline accelerates from -11.4% to -14.6% over four weeks, indicating reduced essential shopping frequency. Households consolidating essential trips reduce incidental retail-and-recreation visits, producing negative RETAIL_REC momentum over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM declined from -11.4% to -14.6% over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days is higher than over last 28 days while GROCERY_PHARM remains below -12%.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility exceeds 7.5% and WORKPLACES mobility falls below -14%, a regime of enforced home-based activity is active. Under this regime, RETAIL_REC remains suppressed over the next four weeks because policy or behavioral constraints limit retail access.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL at 8.0% and WORKPLACES at -15.1% in t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 3 percentage points over the next 28 days when both RESIDENTIAL > 7.5% and WORKPLACES < -14%.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has declined for four consecutive weeks (-17.7% to -22.4%), establishing a strong negative trend. Absent a reversal signal from TRANSIT or WORKPLACES, this trend persists over the next two weeks through path dependence and habit formation.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC declined monotonically from -17.7% to -22.4% over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 percentage points in the first two weeks after t-0w without a corresponding rise in TRANSIT or WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility decline accelerates sharply (-29.3% to -38.9% over four weeks), indicating suppressed outdoor leisure. When outdoor recreation is constrained, consumers substitute toward indoor retail venues, producing a reversal of RETAIL_REC decline over the next four weeks as pent-up demand releases.
candidate_trigger: PARKS decline decelerates (becomes less negative) week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at -38.9% in t-0w, most negative in series
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below -20% over the next 28 days if PARKS mobility begins to recover toward -30% or higher.
